description: Searched in Serbian/Montenegrin for a browsable CBCG list of individual saglasnosti/odobrenja for bank board members and executive directors ('evidencija izdatih saglasnosti', 'saglasnost izvršni direktor banke'). Regulation confirms CBCG keeps an evidence of issued approvals and that the credit-institution register content is prescribed by decision, but no standalone public page enumerating named approvals was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Legal duty confirmed; a public, named, per-person approval list was not found at a discoverable URL.

why_it_matters: If no public per-person list exists, bank leadership changes must be reconstructed from the Registar banaka diff, Council session press releases, Official Gazette entries and bank-side disclosure — a slower and lossier pipeline than the cell rationale assumes.

description: No RSS/Atom or JSON/open-data endpoint was identified for CBCG press releases, Council decisions or vacancy notices during this pass; the site exposes paginated HTML plus a /me/pretraga query endpoint.

result.result_summary: HTML-only collection assumed for all CBCG surfaces.

why_it_matters: Collection must be scraper-based with snapshot diffing, raising fragility and maintenance cost; a feed probe (/rss, /feed, sitemap.xml) should be part of the deterministic verification pass.

description: Exact URLs for the Skupština finance committee (Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet) pages and for CBCG 'Rukovođenje' / 'Unutrašnja organizacija' were inferred from site navigation and news coverage rather than fetched individually; only root or parent URLs are recorded.

result.result_summary: Parent URLs supplied; leaf paths unverified by design (liveness is a separate pass).

why_it_matters: The verification pass must resolve these leaves before the collector is pointed at them, or those signals will silently go uncollected.

description: Search results surfaced CBCG URLs with unusual locale/path prefixes (/c/, /reg/, and one apparently garbled '/luumyaydbzhv.html/' path) alongside the normal /me/ and /e/ prefixes.

result.result_summary: Multiple parallel path prefixes appear to serve the same content; one variant looks like an artefact or mirror.

why_it_matters: Canonicalisation is needed or the collector will produce large volumes of duplicate records for the same press release.

description: The run specifies languages sr/en. Montenegrin (crnogorski) orthography and both Latin and Cyrillic scripts occur on these sources (e.g. zurnal.me exposes a ?script=lat parameter, dan.co.me titles appear in Cyrillic).

result.result_summary: All local-language searching was done in Latin-script Montenegrin/Serbian; Cyrillic query variants were not run.

why_it_matters: Cyrillic-only articles and documents (Dan, some official PDFs) may be missed by a Latin-only keyword matcher.

description: No Universal Capital Bank or Adriatic Bank career page surfaced on the combined four-bank Montenegrin-language query; only a later bank-specific query recovered Adriatic's /me/karijera. Universal Capital Bank's career page was never surfaced in any query.

result.result_summary: UCB career/management pages remain unlocated; only /en/about-the-bank/* paths were observed. Adriatic's karijera page found only on a second, narrower query.

why_it_matters: Broad OR-joined multi-actor queries under-retrieve for smaller Montenegrin banks; each bank needs its own query pass or the smallest banks will be silently missing from the hiring watchlist.

description: For Universal Capital Bank only English-language paths (/en/about-the-bank/...) were returned; no Montenegrin /me/ equivalents appeared, despite searching with local terms 'o nama' and 'menadžment'.

result.result_summary: Could not confirm that ucbank.me publishes a Montenegrin-language about/management tree.

why_it_matters: If UCB genuinely publishes governance only in English, local-language keyword monitoring will never trigger on it and it needs an English-term watch rule as an exception to the sr-first collection design.

description: Lovćen banka's own career and governance page URLs were not returned by search; only the homepage, product pages, an /en/business/search path and a LinkedIn careers post surfaced.

result.result_summary: lovcenbanka.me karijera / upravni odbor paths unconfirmed — this is an unresolved path-discovery problem, not evidence the pages are absent.

why_it_matters: Lovćen is one of the fastest-growing domestic banks; leaving its career path unresolved is a real blind spot in the densest weak-signal layer of this cell.

description: Zapad banka's governance page (/me/banka/rukovodstvo) was found, but no karijera/zapošljavanje path surfaced for zapadbanka.me.

result.result_summary: Leadership source confirmed; hiring source not located for the fastest-growing bank in the system (+19.16% assets in 2025).

why_it_matters: Asset growth of that magnitude almost certainly implies hiring; missing the vacancy channel means missing the clearest build-out signal available in Montenegro right now.

description: Several banks (NLB, Lovćen, Adriatic, Universal Capital, Zapad) run active LinkedIn company pages carrying Montenegrin-language hiring posts, but LinkedIn is login-walled and its ToS forbids scraping.

result.result_summary: Rich corporate-channel content exists but is not lawfully automatable.

why_it_matters: For the smaller banks LinkedIn may be the ONLY corporate channel carrying vacancies; the collection design must budget for manual analyst review rather than assume automated coverage.

description: All URLs in this slice were obtained via search-result metadata and one Wikipedia fetch; no per-URL liveness check was attempted, and none is claimed.

result.result_summary: Every URL is a confidence-scored candidate awaiting the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Two URLs are known-risky: adriaticbank.com/me/karijera was surfaced as http (not https), and ckb.me exposes a legacy .html management path alongside a clean-path equivalent — both may redirect or 404 without meaning the source is dead.

description: The cell's assumed vocabulary ('Vijesti', 'Menadžment') is not uniform across Montenegrin bank sites: Hipotekarna uses 'Obavještenja', Addiko and Prva use 'Saopštenja', Zapad uses 'Rukovodstvo', CKB uses 'Organi upravljanja / Menadžment banke', Erste uses 'Aktuelni konkursi za zapošljavanje', Addiko uses 'Zapošljavanje' rather than 'Karijera'.

result.result_summary: Six distinct label families observed for what are functionally two page types (news, leadership) plus two for careers.

why_it_matters: A crawler keyed only on the seed terms 'Vijesti/Menadžment/Karijera' would miss the majority of these banks; the glossary must carry all variants (obavještenja, saopštenja, rukovodstvo, organi upravljanja, zapošljavanje, konkurs, oglas, radna mjesta).

description: Searched in both English and Serbian for evidence of Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos activity, contracts, offices or hires in Montenegro.

result.result_summary: No Montenegro-specific page, press release or local entity for either global ATM OEM was found; results were generic global ATM-industry articles. Their ME footprint appears to be routed through partners/distributors (e.g. Payten, Printec) rather than own local entities.

why_it_matters: Means direct OEM monitoring is low-yield for ME; the partner/service-provider layer is the correct collection point for ATM estate signals.

description: Searched for a Montenegrin card-personalisation bureau and for named card-personalisation suppliers to Montenegrin banks (sr terms: 'personalizacija platnih kartica', 'dobavljac').

result.result_summary: Only Serbia-based personalisation providers (Zeta, SIS, Cards Print) surfaced, plus ME bank card terms-and-conditions PDFs. No Montenegrin personalisation bureau and no explicit ME bank-supplier pairing was found.

why_it_matters: Card personalisation for ME banks is likely regional or in-house; the cell's card-personalisation sub-question cannot be answered from ME-domestic sources and needs regional vendor monitoring instead.

description: Searched for an explicit 'core banking' vendor-to-Montenegrin-bank attribution (which core system each ME bank runs) in en and sr.

result.result_summary: No public attribution found via general search. Montenegrin systemic banks are private and mostly foreign-group subsidiaries, so core-system choices are made at group level and not disclosed locally.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: core-banking procurement is invisible; indirect proxies (mobile-app package namespaces, e-banking migration notices, CRM reference pages, job ads naming systems) are the only viable route.

description: General web search repeatedly returned Wikipedia bank stubs and CBCG register pages for vendor-oriented queries in both languages.

result.result_summary: Bank-name tokens dominate ranking, crowding out supplier content. Productive results only came from vendor-name-anchored queries (Payten, Printec, Logate, Halcom, Asseco) and portal-name-anchored queries.

why_it_matters: Collection design should be entity-anchored (vendor watchlist) rather than topic-anchored keyword search.

description: LinkedIn (me.linkedin.com company and jobs pages) and EMIS company profiles are the richest people/appointment sources identified.

result.result_summary: LinkedIn is auth-walled and its ToS forbids automated collection; EMIS is subscription-paywalled. Neither was collected.

why_it_matters: The single best leadership-move signal for this cell is not lawfully machine-collectable without licensing; budget for licensed access or manual analyst review.

description: Attempted to locate the Chamber of Economy of Montenegro ICT/banking board membership pages in Serbian.

result.result_summary: Search surfaced only the chamber's supervisory board and contact pages, not an ICT board membership list; the page may exist but was not reachable via search.

why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified rather than absent; needs manual site navigation before concluding the source does not exist.

description: Despite targeted local-language searching, no search result surfaced the official website of Udruženje banaka Crne Gore. Coverage of UBCG reaches us only second-hand via bankar.me, investitor.me, aktuelno.me, MINA and a registry aggregator. The domain listed in this slice (ubcg.info) is an inference from the acronym, not an observed link.

result.result_summary: UBCG has a strong media footprint but a weak/invisible web presence in search; its registered contact in the aggregator is a legacy t-com.me email, consistent with a small secretariat and a minimal or absent site.

why_it_matters: UBCG is the most important pointer in this cell — the authoritative 11-bank member list and the board presidency both live there. Without a resolved domain, membership enumeration must be reconstructed from news, which is slower and lossier.

description: Searched in both Serbian/Montenegrin and English for a standalone Montenegrin fintech or payments association ('fintech udruženje', 'asocijacija za platni promet'). None exists as a distinct organisation.

result.result_summary: The fintech convening function is split between the Central Bank's Fintech Hub, the Chamber of Economy's banking/finance board, and the general IT cluster ICT Cortex.

why_it_matters: There is no single membership list of payments/fintech firms to snowball from; the payments actor universe must be assembled from the CBCG licensed-institution register plus the Chamber board roster plus ICT Cortex members.

description: UPCG's Upravni odbor page and NBOCG's governance pages did not yield a current, dated member roster from search snippets; the most recent named UPCG leadership event found is the April 2023 assembly and the most recent NBOCG assembly president reference is c.2022.

result.result_summary: Rosters exist as pages but their currency could not be established without direct fetch.

why_it_matters: Treating a stale roster as current would produce false 'no change' signals in the leadership-moves workstream.

description: AmCham Montenegro's member listing appears to sit behind an account registration flow (/users/ alongside /register/), and a dev/staging host (dev.amcham.me) also surfaced in results.

result.result_summary: Public board pages are accessible; the full member directory likely is not.

why_it_matters: Full membership enumeration for AmCham may be unobtainable without registering an account, which is out of scope; the board page and news feed must substitute.

description: No Montenegrin-language equivalent term was found in circulation for a 'payments industry association' or 'card scheme member body' — local coverage uses English brand names (Mastercard, Visa) inside Serbian text rather than any local collective noun.

result.result_summary: Local-language search on payments-association terms returns nothing; only English-in-local usage works.

why_it_matters: Queries for this sub-topic must mix English brand tokens into Serbian queries; pure local-language querying under-retrieves on the payments side.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin cards/payments industry event was located. Searches for a Mastercard, Visa or Payten branded forum, conference or partner day in Montenegro returned only consumer card-product marketing pages (mastercard.me campaigns, Hipotekarna banka Mastercard Premium partners) and no event with a speaker or agenda page.

result.result_summary: Searched in Montenegrin for card-scheme and payment-vendor events; zero event-type results. Payments-executive visibility in Montenegro appears to run through INFINTECH, MFM and CBCG events rather than a scheme-run local forum.

why_it_matters: If no local card-scheme forum exists, the cell must rely on cross-sector fintech events for cards/acquiring role signals, and scheme-level personnel (e.g. Visa SEE leadership) will only surface as sponsors/speakers at INFINTECH and MFM.

description: No standalone Montenegrin 'bankarska akademija' (banking academy) institution was found. The local-language query returned Serbian and Croatian institutions instead (Beogradska bankarska akademija, Centar za bankarsku obuku of the Serbian Banking Association, Bankovna akademija at EFZG Zagreb). Montenegro's equivalent function appears to be discharged by UBCG via its ATTF Luxembourg partnership rather than by a domestic academy.

result.result_summary: Local-language search for a Montenegrin banking academy produced only foreign institutions plus the UBCG/ATTF cooperation statement.

why_it_matters: The absence of a domestic academy means there is no single cohort/graduate registry for Montenegrin bank staff; training-derived title signals must be assembled from UBCG, IIA Montenegro and commercial training providers instead. It also means regional Serbian/Croatian academies may be worth tracking for Montenegrin attendees.

description: No banking-specific regional Adriatic/Western Balkans summit with a published Montenegro-heavy speaker roster was found beyond INFINTECH. The 'regional banking summit Adriatic' search returned only political EU-Western Balkans summits (Kotor, Tivat/Porto Montenegro June 2026), which name heads of state rather than bank executives. Kopaonik Business Forum and Zlatibor-type Serbian economic forums did not surface with Montenegrin banking content in this pass.

result.result_summary: English-language regional-summit search returned political summits only; no dedicated Adriatic banking summit identified.

why_it_matters: Regional summits are a likely place for Montenegrin bank executives to appear with current titles; failing to identify them leaves a geographic blind spot in the cell. Worth a dedicated follow-up pass with exact event brand names.

description: No stable, Montenegro-specific award URL was found for The Banker's Bank of the Year, and no confirmed standalone official domain was found for the Tomorrow Conference or the RE:D Montenegro conference. These are recorded at entry-point or coverage-article level and flagged as unverified deep links rather than invented URLs.

result.result_summary: Three candidate sources are recorded via a publisher domain or a media article because their own canonical pages were not located in this pass.

why_it_matters: A downstream verification pass should resolve these to canonical event/award URLs; until then they should not be treated as scrape targets with stable selectors.

description: Euromoney and The Banker both gate their award write-ups behind subscription walls. A single failed or truncated fetch is not evidence the pages are dead; they are live but metered.

result.result_summary: Two award sources flagged blocked=true with blocker_type=paywall.

why_it_matters: Collection design must route around paywalls via the winning banks' own newsrooms and Montenegrin media reproductions, which typically carry the citation plus a named executive quote.

description: No standalone web presence was found for a dedicated Montenegrin banking/finance branch trade union. The sector collective agreement is described as signed by a 'Sindikat finansijskih organizacija Crne Gore', and one media reference points to a 'Sindikat banaka' figure (name Lidija Pejović mentioned in a search summary, unverified), but neither an official site nor a confirmed profile page was located.

result.result_summary: Exact-phrase search for 'Sindikat finansijskih organizacija Crne Gore' returned no dedicated page; only umbrella confederations (SSCG, USSCG) and unrelated unions surfaced.

why_it_matters: The single most valuable primary actor for this cell — the bank workers' union — currently has no confirmed direct source, forcing reliance on confederation and media intermediaries.

description: No specific recent (2024-2026) case of collective redundancy, strike, or branch-closure dispute at a named Montenegrin bank was surfaced by the searches run.

result.result_summary: Searches for tehnološki višak / otpuštanje / zatvaranje filijala at Montenegrin banks returned generic Serbian labour-law explainers rather than Montenegrin bank events; the only bank-workforce case found was the historical Atlas banka bankruptcy coverage on Bankar.me.

why_it_matters: Either such events are genuinely rare/quiet in a small market, or they are reported only in local dailies not well indexed by the search engine used. The collection design must therefore lean on registry-type sources (AMRRS, courts, ZZZCG, inspectorate) rather than search-engine discovery.

description: Serbian-language results dominate Montenegrin labour queries because the languages are near-identical; a large share of hits (paragraf.rs, infostud, zuniclaw, politika.rs, otvorenavratapravosudja.rs, vrh.sud.rs) are Serbian jurisdiction and legally inapplicable to Montenegro.

result.result_summary: Roughly half of the results for 'tehnološki višak' and 'radni spor' queries were Serbian, not Montenegrin.

why_it_matters: Any automated collector must hard-filter by .me domains / Montenegrin institution names, otherwise the corpus will be contaminated with Serbian labour law and Serbian court practice.

description: Neither AMRRS nor ZZZCG appears to publish case- or employer-level records (dispute filings, collective-dismissal notifications) on the open web; only aggregate statistics and news were observed.

result.result_summary: AMRRS site presents mission/contact/annual information; ZZZCG presents statistics and programmes. No searchable per-employer register was found.

why_it_matters: The highest-value adversarial signal for this cell may require freedom-of-information requests rather than scraping; collection design should budget for that.

description: Montenegrin published court decisions are typically anonymised, which may prevent identifying the defendant bank in a labour judgment.

result.result_summary: Court portals (sudovi.me) expose decision listings but party anonymisation is standard regional practice; not verified case-by-case in this run.

why_it_matters: Case-law monitoring may yield the pattern (volume and type of banking-sector labour disputes) without the actor, unless matched with press reporting or docket-level access.

description: The session web-search budget was exhausted before follow-up queries could be run on 'Sindikat banaka' / Lidija Pejović, Vijesti.me and Pobjeda labour sections, Službeni list CG for the current text of the banking branch collective agreement, and per-bank strike history (CKB/OTP, NLB, Hipotekarna, Erste, Addiko, Prva banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Ziraat).

result.result_summary: WebSearch returned a hard budget-exhausted message at 200/200 calls.

why_it_matters: Several named-actor sources for this cell remain undiscovered; a follow-up run with search budget should complete them.

description: No publicly indexed bank-level credit rating reports were found for standalone Montenegrin banks (Hipotekarna banka, Universal Capital Bank, Lovcen banka, Adriatic Bank) from Fitch, Moody's or S&P.

result.result_summary: Two separate searches returned only sovereign ratings for Montenegro and parent-group ratings (Erste, OTP); no Montenegro-domiciled bank issuer rating pages surfaced.

why_it_matters: The premise that rating agencies profile Montenegrin bank management may hold only indirectly, via parent-group reports; A5 leadership signals must lean on IFI and issuer disclosure instead.

description: Rating-agency primary sites (Fitch, Moody's, S&P) and Cbonds require accounts for the substantive commentary.

result.result_summary: Only aggregator mirrors (countryeconomy, tradingeconomics, FX Empire) were freely visible; those carry ratings but no management commentary.

why_it_matters: Any workflow depending on agency prose about bank management needs a licence; free aggregators cannot substitute.

description: No Montenegro-specific IFC investment project in the banking sector was directly surfaced this run.

result.result_summary: The IFC disclosure search returned a Serbian bank project (Banca Intesa Beograd) and the generic portal; the portal's country filter could not be exercised because it is a JS-driven UI and the web-search budget was exhausted.

why_it_matters: IFC's actual Montenegrin banking footprint is unconfirmed; it may be small or channelled via regional facilities. Needs a headless-browser pass against disclosures.ifc.org with country=Montenegro.

description: Local-language searching was performed (Montenegrin/Serbian terms: Crna Gora, banka, projekat, rukovodstvo, izvještaj, Evropska banka za obnovu i razvoj) but only one dedicated sr query could be run before the session's web-search budget was exhausted.

result.result_summary: The single sr query was productive (EBRD Montenegrin-language PSD, MINA, Bankar.me), suggesting substantial untapped local-language depth.

why_it_matters: Local-language coverage of the international layer is under-sampled; sr-language coverage of IMF/World Bank/EU delegation statements is likely richer than captured.

description: The Fitch entity URL and the Addiko investor-relations URL given in candidates are pattern-inferred, not observed in search results.

result.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence_score; a deterministic liveness pass must confirm or replace them.

why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated-URL from being treated as verified.

description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was consumed before I could run planned queries against Croatian and Bosnian business press (poslovni-dnevnik.hr, lider.media, jutarnji/Novac, Klix.ba, Capital.ba, Nezavisne novine, Bizlife.rs, Nova ekonomija, eKapija) and regional wires (Tanjug, Beta, Hina, Fonet, N1 Adria).

result.result_summary: Two final queries returned a budget-exhaustion notice instead of results; those outlets are therefore neither confirmed nor excluded for this cell.

why_it_matters: The Croatian and Bosnian legs of the ex-Yugoslav regional channel are currently unrepresented in this slice, so cross-checking of Montenegrin bank leadership news outside the Serbian/English legs is incomplete.

description: A Bosnian-language/portal-targeted query ('Klix.ba Nezavisne Capital.ba banka Crna Gora preuzimanje banke direktor') returned no on-topic articles — only a Klix.ba Wikipedia entry, a Montenegrin Zakon o bankama PDF and unrelated bank pages.

result.result_summary: No evidence retrieved that Bosnian portals carry Montenegrin bank appointment news at meaningful density.

why_it_matters: Suggests the Bosnian leg of the regional channel may be genuinely thin for Montenegrin bank HR/leadership news, but a single failed query is not proof; it needs re-testing with site-scoped searches before the channel is written off.

description: No regional-media item was found covering rank-and-file jobs/hiring in Montenegrin banks — recruitment, headcount, branch staffing or redundancy following mergers. Serbian-language queries using 'zaposleni' and 'reorganizacija' returned EU progress reports and media-sector analyses, not bank workforce reporting.

result.result_summary: Regional business press covers the ownership/board layer, not the workforce layer.

why_it_matters: Workstream A5 topics 'jobs, hiring' are unlikely to be served by this cell; they will need job boards, bank career pages, LinkedIn or union/statistical sources handled by other cells.

description: No candidate URL in this slice was fetched; all were observed through search-result metadata only. Access status, paywall depth and robots/ToS posture are inferred, not verified.

result.result_summary: All access_status and legal_status values in this slice are hypotheses pending the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents over-trusting the confidence scores; SeeNews and Bloomberg Adria in particular are likely to be partly gated.

description: No Erste Group press release or ad-hoc announcement specifically naming a board appointment or CEO change at Erste Bank AD Podgorica was surfaced in either English or Serbian searches.

result.result_summary: Erste's group press room and IR feed exist and are trackable, but Montenegro-specific governance items appear rare — Erste Bank Podgorica is a small unit (~13.8% share, ~420 staff) below the group's ad-hoc materiality threshold.

why_it_matters: The cell's core hypothesis (group English disclosure precedes local statement) holds strongly for Addiko and NLB, but likely fails for Erste; Montenegro Erste leadership changes will probably have to be caught locally (CBCG, bankar.me, roster diffs) rather than at group level.

description: A guessed NLB Group press-centre URL (https://www.nlbgroup.com/int-en/press-centre) returned HTTP 404.

result.result_summary: The correct paths were then recovered from the site's own navigation: /int-en/media-center/press-releases and /int-en/investor-relations/investor-news.

why_it_matters: Records that the canonical NLB paths are the media-center ones; any collector built against a 'press-centre' path will silently collect nothing.

description: No KAP (Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu) filing naming Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica board changes was found; searches using the Turkish term 'Karadağ' also returned nothing filing-level.

result.result_summary: Ziraat's Montenegro unit is documented only via group subsidiary pages and annual reports, plus CBCG press releases that happen to list attending managers by name.

why_it_matters: For Ziraat, the earliest observable channel is likely the Montenegrin regulator, not the Turkish parent — inverting this cell's usual assumption; a KAP collector may not be worth building.

description: Serbian-language searching did not confirm that Alta Pay Group owns or controls Lovćen banka AD Podgorica; Alta Pay Group was only confirmed as ~76% owner of Alta banka a.d. (Belgrade).

result.result_summary: The 'Alta Pay / regional owners' element of the cell definition is therefore partly unverified for Montenegro; Lovćen banka's own shareholder-notice page was found instead and is the safer anchor.

why_it_matters: Building a parent-group watchlist on an unconfirmed ownership link would produce a permanently empty collector; the actor map needs the CBCG register as its source of truth.

description: No Serbian/Montenegrin-language version of NLB Group's or OTP Group's parent press room carrying subsidiary appointment news was found; group communications for Montenegro appear to be English-only at parent level, with Montenegrin text only on the local bank sites (nlb.me, ckb.me).

result.result_summary: Local-language coverage of this cell therefore has to come from the subsidiary sites, CBCG and bankar.me rather than from the parents.

why_it_matters: Defines the language architecture of the cell: parent = English, local = sr; a bilingual matching layer is required to link the two into one event.

description: The CBCG register of e-money institutions and their agents was fetched directly and states that no e-money institution is currently entered ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac').

result.result_summary: Zero licensed EMIs in Montenegro at time of scouting; the EMI half of this cell's actor universe is currently empty, so all EMI-specific hiring/leadership queries return nothing by construction.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort on a non-existent actor set, and reframes the EMI register as a market-entry tripwire rather than an ongoing hiring feed. Any future first entrant is a high-value signal.

description: A Montenegrin-language search on card processing and acquiring ('procesiranje kartica akvajering Crna Gora kompanija Podgorica') returned no relevant payment-industry results — output was dominated by unrelated retail, construction and telecom hits.

result.result_summary: No standalone Montenegro-domiciled card processor or acquirer surfaced via local-language search. The processing layer appears to be served by regional vendors (Payten/Asseco SEE, which does have a Podgorica office) and by banks' in-house acquiring, rather than by a locally registered specialist.

why_it_matters: Means the acquiring/processing part of this cell must be tracked through regional vendor careers pages and bank-adjacent sources rather than a Montenegrin register. Also flags 'akvajering' as a low-yield search term in this market.

description: Several otherwise-plausible local terms proved noisy or unproductive. 'Akvajering' returned essentially no payments results. 'Moneta' collides with generic monetary vocabulary and foreign brands. 'Alta' collides with Alta Banka / Alta Group in Serbia. 'Transfer' in Montenegrin web space is overwhelmingly dominated by airport/tourist transfer services.

result.result_summary: Query design for this cell must anchor on full registered legal names from the CBCG register rather than on generic payments vocabulary.

why_it_matters: Directly shapes the collection query set: name-anchored queries plus the term 'platna institucija' are reliable; generic payments nouns are not.

description: For the licensed payment institutions in the register, no dedicated karijera/careers page was confirmed on any company site during this pass; hiring surfaced instead via the trade portal bankar.me and via job boards.

result.result_summary: PI hiring in Montenegro appears to be advertised through third-party channels rather than owned careers pages, consistent with employers of roughly 8-30 staff.

why_it_matters: Collection design should weight third-party job feeds (bankar.me, ZZZCG) far above company careers-page crawling for this cell, while still diffing company sites for leadership/about-page changes.

description: The CBCG payment-systems register page carried no operator names in its HTML body; the actual list is only inside a linked 'Pregled registra' PDF that was not opened in this pass.

result.result_summary: Payment-system operator identities for Montenegro remain unresolved at slice level — a known, addressable gap rather than an absence.

why_it_matters: The infrastructure-operator employer layer is currently unmapped for this cell; it needs one targeted PDF retrieval to close.

description: No Montenegrin outlet was identified that systematically reports appointments at non-bank payment institutions specifically. Bankar.me covers finance-sector appointments and job ads but its leadership coverage skews heavily to banks (Prva banka, Komercijalna banka, Adriatic banka) rather than PIs.

result.result_summary: Leadership-move coverage for PIs is thin in local media; the register/CRPS route is likely the only reliable one.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: this cell's leadership signal will come from statutory filings with a lag, not from press, so CRPS diffing must be treated as the primary detector rather than a backstop.

description: No Montenegro-specific 'people moves' / appointments column or newsletter for fintech-crypto was found in either Serbian/Montenegrin or English.

result.result_summary: Searches for appointment terminology returned general ecosystem and regulator content, no dedicated moves tracker.

why_it_matters: Leadership-move detection for this cell must be assembled from company pages, LinkedIn and general news rather than from any single feed.

description: Direct queries for a fintech opening a Podgorica office and hiring a country manager returned no such concrete announcement.

result.result_summary: Only an adjacent example (Infinum's Podgorica office with a named managing director) and generic ecosystem pages surfaced.

why_it_matters: Confirms that office-opening/country-manager signals in ME are sparse and must be caught via job boards and company office pages, not press.

description: Highest-value people-move sources (LinkedIn, Wellfound, Tracxn, Dealroom) are login-walled or paywalled.

result.result_summary: Only summary/snippet data reachable without accounts or licences.

why_it_matters: Budget or manual-analyst capacity is required; automated collection alone will under-detect this cell.

description: Montenegrin startup media is thin and partly dormant — several of the most relevant Digitalizuj.Me items surfaced are from 2019-2022.

result.result_summary: Recent (2025-2026) local startup hiring coverage was not surfaced in this pass.

why_it_matters: Freshness of local-language media coverage must be verified before relying on it as a primary detector.

description: Noisy terms identified: 'Coinis' (adtech, not crypto despite the name), 'Flash' (generic), 'Spark' (a Serbian youth conference at sparkconf.rs distinct from Montenegro's spark.me), 'startap/startup Crna Gora' (dominated by policy and grant content).

result.result_summary: Several searches returned off-target results driven by these terms.

why_it_matters: Collection filters need disambiguation rules or precision will be poor.

description: The ZZZCG vacancy listing page (/srm/) was fetched and inspected directly. It offers rich HTML filters and stable per-vacancy URLs but exposes no RSS feed, API or bulk export in the page content observed.

result.result_summary: Collection from the state bureau must be HTML crawling across ~126 paginated result pages plus per-oglas detail fetches; no machine-readable feed was found.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic engineering expectations for the single most authoritative source in this cell, and means change-detection must be built on page diffs rather than feed timestamps.

description: bankar.me/category/oglasi-za-posao/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with an empty body to a plain fetcher, while its article URLs (e.g. the CKB information-security expert vacancy) appear normally in search indexes.

result.result_summary: Treated as bot-defended-but-live, NOT dead. Liveness is unverified here and left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Bankar.me is the only banking-sector-specific vacancy feed found for Montenegro; wrongly recording it as dead would remove the highest-signal-to-noise source in the cell.

description: Searched in Serbian for itemised vacancy listings at several domestic banks. Universal Capital Bank and Prva banka Crne Gore publish only open CV-intake channels (an email address) rather than enumerated openings; no vacancy list page was found for either.

result.result_summary: For these employers no first-party vacancy stream exists to monitor; their hiring must be inferred from ZZZCG filings, boards, agencies or trade press.

why_it_matters: Prevents a false coverage claim — a silent careers page is not evidence of no hiring, and the analytic method must differ per employer.

description: Local-language searches combining vacancy terms with payments-specific Montenegrin vocabulary ('platni promet', 'kartično poslovanje', 'fintech specijalista') returned only generic portal homepages, no payments-specific vacancy listings or a payments-specialised board.

result.result_summary: No dedicated payments-sector job board exists for Montenegro; payments roles must be extracted by keyword from general boards and bank career pages.

why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot rely on a pre-filtered payments vacancy feed and must invest in a payments/IT-in-finance keyword taxonomy applied across general sources.

description: Searches for 'mojposao' and 'posao.me' surfaced mojposao.hr, a Croatian portal, rather than a Montenegrin site; no Montenegrin portal at those exact names was confirmed.

result.result_summary: Regional name collisions produce false positives; Montenegrin equivalents are zaposli.me, mnejobs.me, prekoveze.me and posao.crna.gora.me.

why_it_matters: Guards a downstream collector against pointing a Montenegro feed at Croatian vacancy data.

description: LinkedIn job search for Podgorica/Montenegro banking and PCI DSS/compliance roles returned only aggregate counts (~202 Podgorica jobs, ~91 Montenegro IT jobs) via search snippets; individual matching vacancies were not retrievable without a session, and LinkedIn ToS prohibits automated collection.

result.result_summary: LinkedIn is high-value but must be handled as manual/licensed access, not as a scraped feed.

why_it_matters: Prevents planning a collection pipeline that would be both technically blocked and contractually non-compliant.

description: No LinkedIn company page could be surfaced for Addiko Bank AD Podgorica, Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica or Zapad banka AD Podgorica via external search; only individual employee profiles appeared (Addiko surfaced solely through an executive mention).

result.result_summary: Employee-profile-only visibility for at least three licensed ME banks.

why_it_matters: Coverage of the licensed-bank universe via company pages is incomplete; monitoring for these actors must fall back to individual profiles or non-LinkedIn sources.

description: LinkedIn's content/people search — the mechanism that actually surfaces 'new role' announcements — is unreachable without an authenticated session, and external search engines index those posts only sparsely. Local-language phrase queries ('nova uloga', 'sa zadovoljstvom objavljujem') returned almost no genuine ME banking announcement posts through an external engine.

result.result_summary: The highest-value signal in this cell is only reachable from inside an authenticated LinkedIn session.

why_it_matters: Any collection design that assumes crawlable LinkedIn post search will fail; the cell requires an analyst account and manual saved searches.

description: No LinkedIn school/alumni page was surfaced for Ekonomski fakultet Podgorica (Univerzitet Crne Gore); only Facebook, X and Instagram presences appeared. LinkedIn's Alumni tool is itself login-gated.

result.result_summary: Alumni-based discovery of banking staff could not be established from outside LinkedIn.

why_it_matters: The alumni route — a strong way to enumerate a small market's banking cohort — remains unvalidated and needs an authenticated check.

description: Beyond Payten/ASEE, no LinkedIn company page for a Montenegro-licensed non-bank payment institution was confirmed; the ME payments startups named by Tracxn (PencePay, XCHPay.me, LocalPay, Sharej, 4On) were not individually verified as having LinkedIn pages in this pass.

result.result_summary: PSP-side LinkedIn coverage is thin and unverified.

why_it_matters: Sector scope is 'both' (banking and payments); the payments half of this cell is materially weaker than the banking half.

description: Several actors have more than one LinkedIn slug (Hipotekarna Banka: /hipotekarna-banka and /hipotekarna-banka-official-page-; CBCG: /centralna-banka-crne-gore and /central-bank-of-montenegro).

result.result_summary: Duplicate/legacy company pages exist per actor.

why_it_matters: Monitoring only one slug risks missing posts; deduplication rules are needed in the source registry.

description: The cell brief names 'Analitika' as a target outlet. The domain analitika.me does NOT serve that outlet: a request to https://www.analitika.me/ redirects to https://fv88.llc/, an unrelated third-party site. The Montenegrin outlet is Portal Analitika at portalanalitika.me, whose business vertical is /abiznis.

result.result_summary: analitika.me -> 302/redirect chain terminating at fv88.llc (HTTP 200 on the wrong host); portalanalitika.me -> HTTP 200 with /abiznis, /najnovije, /politika, /drustvo sections.

why_it_matters: Collecting analitika.me would ingest content from an unrelated (likely gambling/parked) domain and would silently produce zero real Montenegrin coverage while appearing healthy. The source register must pin portalanalitika.me and explicitly blocklist analitika.me.

description: The available web search is US-indexed and returns almost no results from .me news domains even for well-formed Serbian/Montenegrin queries. Local-language queries about Montenegrin bank appointments repeatedly returned Wikipedia, Croatian, Serbian and Slovenian results instead of the Montenegrin outlets actually named in the query.

result.result_summary: Five separate sr-language queries (Vijesti banka novi izvršni direktor; Pobjeda smjena rukovodstva otkazi; CdM reorganizacija zatvaranje filijala; Dan imenovan glavni izvršni direktor; sindikat radnici otkazi) each returned zero on-target articles from the named outlet. Only Bankar.me was reliably indexed.

why_it_matters: Source discovery and, later, content collection for this cell cannot rely on this search engine. Collection must be built on direct site crawling, RSS polling and each outlet's own on-site search endpoint (e.g. vijesti.me/pretraga?q=, portalanalitika.me/pretraga) rather than on general web search.

description: Several primary outlets refused the default HTML fetcher. dan.co.me returned HTTP 403 on both / and /ekonomija even with a desktop-Chrome User-Agent; vijesti.me HTML could not be retrieved at all; cdm.me, mina.news and bankar.me category pages returned 403 while their RSS feeds returned 200.

result.result_summary: 403/blocked at HTML layer for dan.co.me, vijesti.me, cdm.me/ekonomija, mina.news business section, bankar.me/category/*; 200 for bankar.me/feed/, cdm.me/feed/, mina.news/feed/, vijesti.me/rss, vijesti.me/rss/vijesti.

why_it_matters: These are bot-defence hypotheses, not dead sources — RSS success on the same hosts proves the sites are live. The collection design should prefer feeds and, where no feed exists (dan.co.me), budget for a headless-browser fetcher. Do not mark any of these as dead.

description: No economy/banking-scoped RSS feed was found for the largest outlets. vijesti.me/rss/ekonomija returned 404 (only the site-wide /rss and /rss/vijesti exist); antenam.net/rss returned 404; ekonomist.me/feed/ returned 404; pobjeda.me/feed returned 200 but yielded no parseable item titles.

result.result_summary: Section-scoped feeds absent; site-wide feeds are high-volume and heavily mixed with sport/entertainment (the cdm.me and mina.news feeds sampled were dominated by sport and world news).

why_it_matters: Feed polling alone will bury banking personnel items in noise. The pipeline needs a keyword/actor classifier applied to site-wide feeds, plus URL-path filtering on /ekonomija, rather than assuming a clean sector feed exists.

description: Despite targeted local-language searching, no Montenegrin outlet was found to run a standing, named 'personnel column' (a recurring 'kadrovske promjene' / 'ljudi i karijere' rubric) of the kind common in larger markets. The closest observed is Bankar.me publishing periodic one-off survey articles on changes in bank governing structures.

result.result_summary: Searches for kadrovske promjene rubrics returned only individual Bankar.me articles, not a persistent section URL.

why_it_matters: Collection cannot subscribe to a single high-precision personnel rubric; it must instead run recall-oriented keyword sweeps across general economy sections, which raises the volume and the need for filtering.

description: English-language reporting on Montenegrin bank layoffs, restructuring and branch closures is effectively absent. English searching returned only expat banking guides, thebanks.eu sector aggregation and generic sector-consolidation background, with no outlet-level personnel reporting.

result.result_summary: The English query returned nomadcapitalist, thebanks.eu, montenegroguides and an IMF letter of intent — no news reporting on Montenegrin bank personnel or restructuring events.

why_it_matters: Confirms that Serbian/Montenegrin-language collection is not optional for this cell but the only viable channel. Any English-only monitoring configuration for ME would be structurally blind.

description: Automated fetch of http://www.pretraga.crps.me/ failed with an OpenSSL TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR on the HTTPS upgrade.

result.result_summary: Could not read the CRPS search form, so the exact search fields, whether officer names are shown without login, and whether any JSON endpoint exists remain unconfirmed. Hypothesis: live but TLS/bot-unfriendly to this fetcher, not dead.

why_it_matters: CRPS is the cell's keystone source; the collection pipeline design depends on whether officer data is exposed to unauthenticated queries and in what shape.

description: Searched in Serbian for a CRPS change bulletin / RSS / 'objave o promjenama' style feed equivalent to Croatia's or Serbia's registry announcement streams.

result.result_summary: No evidence found of a public chronological feed of CRPS registration changes; monitoring appears to require per-entity polling and diffing.

why_it_matters: Rules out an event-stream architecture; the collector must maintain a watchlist and snapshot-diff, which sets cost and latency expectations.

description: Probed for hypothesised Montenegrin company-data portals 'bizniscrnagora' and 'boniteti.me'.

result.result_summary: Neither returned evidence of existence for Montenegro; CompanyWall.me is the dominant local-language credit/company-data aggregator instead.

why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated source entry and concentrates aggregator effort on CompanyWall plus the English-language bulk vendors.

description: Montenegroberza / MNSE issuer-announcement section was not directly opened in this run; only the exchange's existence and two candidate domains (montenegroberza.com, mnse.me) were established from search results.

result.result_summary: Exact announcements URL and whether an RSS/feed exists is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: Exchange disclosure is likely the fastest legal signal of bank board changes; the pipeline needs the real endpoint before it can be scheduled.

description: Montenegro's Law on Credit Institutions moved banks to a two-tier system, replacing 'izvršni direktor' + 'odbor direktora' with 'uprava' + 'nadzorni odbor'.

result.result_summary: Both vocabularies coexist across historical filings and current pages.

why_it_matters: Any keyword-based extraction over CRPS, the gazette or bank pages must match BOTH term sets or it will silently miss changes on one side of the transition.

description: The Ministry of Finance site (gov.me/mif) was fetched and shows news, javne nabavke, javne rasprave and javni pozivi, but NO dedicated vacancies/konkursi section.

result.result_summary: Ministry vacancies are not self-published; they route to the central register at uzk.gov.me/oglasi. Collection design must not expect a ministry-level jobs feed.

why_it_matters: Prevents building a per-ministry crawler that would silently return zero hiring signal.

description: No careers/konkursi page could be located for Investiciono-razvojni fond (irfcg.me) via local-language or English search.

result.result_summary: IRF leadership changes are traceable (gov.me kadrovska pitanja, RTCG), but IRF's own operational hiring channel is unconfirmed - it may use ZZZCG/prekoveze.me instead.

why_it_matters: A gap in staff-level hiring signal for a state-linked lender; needs a manual site crawl to settle.

description: No dedicated careers/oglasi page for Pošta Crne Gore was found in search; only the Menadžment page and in-house 'Poštanski glasnik' PDFs surfaced.

result.result_summary: Postal vacancies, including payment-counter and platni promet roles, likely go via ZZZCG rather than postacg.me. Unverified - not a dead end.

why_it_matters: Pošta is the cell's most direct public-sector payments actor; missing its hiring feed would blunt the payments angle.

description: English-language search for Montenegro Ministry of Finance treasury vacancies/appointments returned only generic institutional and Wikipedia/OECD material - no vacancy or appointment records.

result.result_summary: English is not a viable discovery language for this cell's primary signal; all operative notices are Montenegrin-language.

why_it_matters: Confirms local-language collection is mandatory, not optional, for the public-sector route.

description: uzk.gov.me/oglasi listing links are built as ./oglasi.php?s=<opaque base64-ish token> rather than stable readable URLs.

result.result_summary: Tokenised links may be session- or rotation-dependent; hardcoded deep links risk breaking.

why_it_matters: Collector must re-resolve listing links from the index page each run; a 404/empty result on a stored token is not evidence the source is dead.

description: RTCG reported that state-administration competitions can be blocked/frozen pending adoption of the Budget Law and the Kadrovski plan, and that senior-management competitions only open after those acts plus internal systematisation acts.

result.result_summary: Zero-vacancy periods in the public route are often legal/procedural, not a real absence of demand.

why_it_matters: Prevents misreading a quiet quarter at uzk.gov.me as a decline in state-side banking/payments activity.

description: Several cell terms are ambiguous across borders and sectors: 'Ministarstvo finansija' also returns Bosnia/Serbia/USK results; 'javni konkurs' returns grant/EU-fund calls (eufondovikonkursi.com, CRNVO) not job vacancies; 'Fond' collides with Fond PIO, Fond zdravstva, investment funds.

result.result_summary: Raw seed terms produce heavy false positives without a Crna Gora / .me domain and institution-name constraint.

why_it_matters: Query design must pin the country and the exact institution name, and separate 'konkurs' for grants from 'konkurs' for posts.
